name: become-context
description: Establishes and maintains the single source of truth every other Become marketing skill loads first — product truth and hub-by-hub feature inventory, brand system, voice rules, ICP and personas, positioning summary, honest proof points, the hard constraint list, and the repo asset inventory — written to marketing/.agents/become-context.md. Use when the user says "set up marketing context," "what is Become again," "update the brand doc," "our messaging is inconsistent," "the copy keeps making things up about the product," or "remind yourself what we're selling." Use this before any other marketing skill, and re-run it whenever the product ships something new. For the category decision see positioning; for channel sequencing see marketing-plan.
sections_hint: Purpose: produce/refresh marketing/.agents/become-context.md, the anchor document
Process assessment gate: does the doc exist, how stale, what shipped since, what is unverified

Frameworks > The twelve sections of the context document (overview, product truth by hub, ICP, personas, pains, competitive alternatives, differentiation, objections and anti-persona, customer language verbatim, brand and voice, proof points we can honestly make, goals)
Frameworks > Verified vs assumed: every claim tagged [verified in repo] / [verified with Jon] / [assumption, unvalidated]
Frameworks > Asset inventory table (copy the verified paths from _conventions.md section 12)
Frameworks > Document version + Changelog convention, newest first, one line per change
Become-specific rules: this doc is the ONLY place product truth is edited; downstream skills read, never redefine
Quality bar: no invented feature, no invented pricing, every path resolves, changelog updated

name: positioning
description: Locks Become's market category and competitive frame with the April Dunford positioning canvas — true competitive alternatives, unique attributes with proof, value themes, the behavioural traits of who cares most, and the frame of reference we want to be filed under. Use when the user says "how do we position this," "what category are we in," "we sound like every other fitness app," "who are we actually competing with," "why would someone pick us over MyFitnessPal," "should we call ourselves a tracker," or "our messaging feels generic." Use this before writing headlines, naming a category, or planning a launch. For a per-competitor teardown see competitor-analysis; for what we ask people to say yes to see offer-design; for the channel plan that follows see marketing-plan.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which best-fit users, what baggage to shed, which alternatives are real (including "nothing" and the Notes app)
Frameworks > The positioning canvas, five components plus optional trends, as a fillable table
Frameworks > The ten-step process in order, with the failure mode of skipping each
Frameworks > Choosing the frame of reference: candidate frames scored on where our strengths look obvious
Frameworks > From canvas to messaging: value theme becomes headline, attribute becomes proof

Become-specific rules: the draft canvas (alternatives = Notes app plus YouTube, a stitched app stack, an in-person trainer, an AI chatbot; attributes = coach-built phases plus AI generator, LIVE mode that logs the set as you train, whole-plate photo logging, every hub in one dashboard, weekly recap; themes = one app instead of five, a coach's structure without the standing appointment, evidence about yourself not vibes) is DRAFT and must be validated, not quoted as settled
Become-specific rules: do not frame as "workout tracker" (loses on depth to Hevy/Strong)
Quality bar: every attribute has proof in the product, no attribute is a benefit in disguise

name: marketing-plan
description: Builds a sequenced, resourced marketing plan for Become — goals worth chasing, channel bets ordered by expected return for a free coach-led PWA, 30/60/90 phasing, the asset manifest with the skill that produces each item, and the numbers that decide whether a bet continues or dies. Use when the user says "what should we do next," "make a marketing plan," "where should we spend our time," "we have no strategy," "what's the 90-day plan," "which channel first," or "how do we get users." Use this even when the ask is vague or the user only describes a feeling of being behind. For the positioning input it depends on see positioning; for a dated post schedule see content-calendar; for one launch moment see launch-campaign; for what to measure see analytics-tracking.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: what is the actual constraint (time, money, distribution, product readiness), current baseline numbers, who executes

Frameworks > Channel bets ranked for Become: organic social, coach-led audience, SEO/GEO, directories and launch surfaces, referral, paid social, community. Each with cost, time-to-signal, ceiling, and the reason it does or does not fit a free PWA
Frameworks > The 30/60/90 shape: prove one channel, then compound, then buy
Frameworks > One-bet-per-quarter discipline and the kill criteria
Frameworks > Asset manifest: every plan line names the producing skill
Become-specific rules: no paid budget assumed; no pricing lever exists; Jon's audience is the highest-leverage owned asset; team is small so plans must be executable by one person plus agents
Quality bar: every bet has a metric, a review date, and a kill rule

name: offer-design
description: Designs what Become asks a visitor to say yes to, given that the app is free today and no pricing exists — the primary offer, the lowest-friction first step, value framing without a price anchor, honest urgency, and the risk reversal a magic-link signup already gives us. Use when the user says "what's our offer," "what should the CTA be," "how do we make signup feel worth it," "should we gate anything," "we can't just say free forever," "how do we create urgency without lying," or "why would anyone sign up today." Never invents pricing, tiers, trial lengths, or discounts. For the words that express the offer see copywriting; for the flow after the yes see signup-activation; for the shareable version see referral-program.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which audience, which surface, what is the single next action, what proof exists to back it
Frameworks > The offer stack for a free product: the promise, the first step, the time cost, the proof, the reversal
Frameworks > Value equation without price: dream outcome, perceived likelihood, time to first result, effort and sacrifice
Frameworks > Honest urgency ladder (a real cohort start, a real program drop, a real week boundary) versus fake urgency (fake countdowns, fake scarcity, invented founder pricing) with the ❌/✅ pairs
Frameworks > First-step design: magic link, no credit card, one email field, and what that buys us in objection handling
Become-specific rules: "Free today" is the only permitted price statement; never imply a future price; never promise a timeline or a pound count
Quality bar: the offer survives the question "is every word of this literally true today"

name: competitor-analysis
description: Runs a structured teardown of a named fitness, nutrition, or mindset competitor — MyFitnessPal, Hevy, Strong, Fitbod, Ladder, STNDRD, Whoop, Strava, Cal AI, Headspace, or a local coach-led alternative — covering positioning and category claim, feature surface versus ours, pricing and monetization, acquisition channels, creative and content system, review-mined weaknesses, and the specific gap Become can own. Use when the user says "how does X compare," "what is Ladder doing," "who else does photo food logging," "competitor research," "why would someone pick us over Hevy," "is anyone else itemizing a whole plate from one photo," or drops a competitor URL with no instruction. For our own category decision see positioning; for their visual ad patterns specifically see inspo-library.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which competitor, which question we are answering, is this a one-off or a refresh
Process: research method — site, pricing page, app listings, review mining, ad libraries, social accounts — with the note that WebSearch and WebFetch are the tools and every claim gets a source line
Frameworks > The eight-axis teardown table
Frameworks > Review mining: how to pull the recurring one-star complaint into our differentiation
Frameworks > Gap analysis: where their strength is structural (do not attack) versus positional (attack)
Frameworks > Output: a comparison table plus three sentences we can honestly say about the difference
Become-specific rules: never publish a comparison claim we cannot verify today; never quote a competitor price without the date checked; competitor screenshots stay internal
Quality bar: every row cites a source with a date

name: copywriting
description: Writes new Become marketing copy from a blank page — landing sections, feature blocks, hero and subhead sets, ad copy, email and push subject lines, listing text, brand-voice social captions, share-sheet lines, and one-liners — in the Become voice, delivered with annotations and labelled alternatives. Use when the user says "write the hero," "we need copy for the nutrition section," "give me headline options," "write an ad for LIVE mode," "what should this button say," "make this page," or "I need words for this." Use this even when the user only describes a feature and expects copy back. For improving copy that already exists see copy-editing; for diagnosing why a page does not convert see landing-cro; for Jon speaking in the first person see coach-brand-voice.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which surface and its length limits, which audience state, which single idea, what proof is available, what the next action is
Frameworks > Message hierarchy: one idea per block, benefit then mechanism then proof
Frameworks > Headline formulas with weak-vs-strong pairs (outcome without the pain, the concrete noun, the specific moment, the honest contrast)
Frameworks > Feature-to-value translation table for each hub, using the real mechanic (LIVE mode logs the set as you train, the photo itemizes the plate, the recap writes your week back to you)
Frameworks > CTA writing: verb plus object plus payoff; weak-vs-strong table
Frameworks > Length specs per surface (hero, subhead, section, card, button, subject line, push title and body, OG description)
Output buckets: Page copy / Annotations / Alternatives A-B-C with rationale / Meta content
Become-specific rules: no pricing, no results claims, no fabricated proof, no banned words, near-zero em dashes, The Becoming at most one mention

name: landing-cro
description: Diagnoses and improves conversion on become.redbtn.io and other entry surfaces — value-proposition clarity, section order, what happens above the fold on a 390px screen, proof placement, CTA friction, magic-link objections, form design, and load-speed drag — and returns prioritized fixes with test hypotheses. Use when the user says "the landing page isn't converting," "nobody signs up," "audit our landing page," "is our hero clear," "should the CTA be higher," "there's too much scrolling," "the page feels flat," or just pastes a URL and asks what is wrong. For writing new words see copywriting; for tightening existing words see copy-editing; for everything after the click see signup-activation; for actually running the test see ab-testing.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which traffic source, which device, what the visitor already believes, what the current page does (read webapp/components/landing/)

Frameworks > Seven dimensions in order of impact, each with Check-for / Common issues / Strong patterns: 1 value proposition clarity, 2 above-the-fold on mobile, 3 conversion action and friction, 4 proof and credibility, 5 section order and narrative flow, 6 objection handling, 7 speed and motion cost
Frameworks > Mobile-first specifics: 390x844, thumb zone, safe-area insets, sticky CTA, scroll depth before the first ask
Frameworks > The magic-link objection set (no password, will the email arrive, what if I close the tab) and how the page pre-answers it
Frameworks > Proof we can legitimately show: real product captures, coach credentials, the mechanism itself. Not: counts, testimonials, star ratings
Output buckets: Quick wins / High-impact changes / Test ideas / Copy alternatives with rationale
Become-specific rules: cite real component paths; screenshots only from screenshots/v2; light AND dark must both work

name: copy-editing
description: Edits copy that already exists down to the Become voice — cuts fluff and banned phrasing, strips AI slop and em dashes, replaces abstractions with the concrete noun, fixes rhythm and reading level, and flags any line that breaks the no-fabrication, no-pricing, or responsible-claims rules. Returns a marked before-and-after with a one-line reason per change. Use when the user says "tighten this," "this sounds like AI," "make it sound like us," "too wordy," "punch this up," "review this copy," "does this sound right," or pastes a draft with no instruction at all. For writing from scratch see copywriting; for page structure and conversion see landing-cro; for Jon's first-person register see coach-brand-voice.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which surface, which voice register (product second person vs Jon first person), what must not change (claims, links, length limits)

Frameworks > The five edit passes in order: 1 truth pass (claims, pricing, features that do not exist), 2 slop pass (banned words, em dashes, hedges, throat-clearing), 3 concreteness pass (abstraction to noun), 4 rhythm pass (sentence length variance, front-loaded verbs), 5 fit pass (length limits, scannability)
Frameworks > The banned list with a replacement for each entry, not just a prohibition
Frameworks > AI-slop tells: tricolon addiction, "not just X but Y," "in a world where," symmetrical clause pairs, adjective stacking, em dash overuse
Frameworks > When NOT to edit: voice-authentic roughness in Jon's first-person copy
Output buckets: Marked diff / Reason per change / Two alternate versions (tighter, warmer) / Claims flagged for verification
Quality bar: word count reduced, zero banned words, every claim traceable

name: signup-activation
description: Optimizes everything after the click — the magic-link signup flow, inbox and deliverability friction, the verify-and-return handoff between tabs, onboarding questions and their order, first-session activation, the PWA install prompt, and the day-1 to day-7 loop that turns a signup into a logged workout. Use when the user says "people sign up but never come back," "onboarding is too long," "the magic link is confusing," "improve activation," "what's our aha moment," "nobody installs the PWA," "day 2 retention is bad," or "they stall on the first screen." For pre-click page conversion see landing-cro; for the emails in the sequence see email-lifecycle; for the nudges see push-notifications; for the events behind the funnel see analytics-tracking.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: where exactly users drop (signup submitted, link clicked, onboarding started, first log), on which device, from which source
Frameworks > The activation funnel stages with the one metric each: email submitted, link delivered, link clicked, account created, onboarding completed, first meaningful action, day-7 return

Frameworks > Magic-link specific friction, in order of impact: wrong-tab confusion, inbox delay, spam placement, expired token, mobile mail app in-app browser. Check-for / Common issues / Strong patterns for each
Frameworks > Time-to-value: what is the fastest honest first win in Become (a generated session, a logged plate photo, a first mood check-in)
Frameworks > Onboarding question economics: every question must change what the app shows next or be cut
Frameworks > PWA install prompt timing: never on first load, ask after the first earned win
Output buckets: Quick wins / High-impact changes / Test ideas / Copy alternatives
Become-specific rules: cite real routes (/login, /verify, /onboarding, /dashboard); no fake progress bars; no dark patterns

name: web-app-listing
description: Produces Become's listings for the surfaces a PWA actually lives on — Product Hunt, AlternativeTo, BetaList, PWA and web-app directories, fitness-tool roundups, Reddit and forum resource threads — plus the install-surface metadata that stands in for a store page, including manifest name and description, install-prompt copy, share-sheet text, Open Graph and Twitter cards, and the short and long blurbs each directory asks for. Use when the user says "write our Product Hunt listing," "list us on directories," "we need an app store description," "what goes in the manifest," "write our install prompt," "how do people find us if we're not in the App Store," or "we need a tagline for this listing." For the launch moment around a submission see launch-campaign; for how these listings get cited by AI answers see seo-geo.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which surface, its exact character limits and required fields, whether a live account is needed, submission rules
Frameworks > The listing asset kit: name, 40-char tagline, 60-char, 160-char, 260-char, and long descriptions; category and tags; gallery order; first comment
Frameworks > Directory tiers for a free PWA, ranked by realistic referral and citation value, each with format notes and gotchas
Frameworks > Install-surface metadata as our store page: manifest fields, install prompt, share text, OG and Twitter cards, and the exact files that hold them
Frameworks > Gallery rules: which of the 15 v2 captures to use, in which order, light or dark per surface
Output buckets: The listing (all fields, at length) / Gallery manifest / Submission checklist / Alternatives for the tagline
Become-specific rules: we are a PWA, not an app-store app. No ratings, no download counts, no pricing tier. Never write "(beta)" into a listing

name: social-strategy
description: Sets Become's organic social operating system — platform mix and cadence, the Reels-for-reach plus carousels-for-trust split, content pillars mapped to the five product hubs, share and save mechanics that buy unconnected reach, how the Become handle and Jon's handle divide the work, and what to actually measure. Use when the user says "what should we post," "grow our Instagram," "we post and nothing happens," "how often should we post," "TikTok or Instagram," "what are our content pillars," "our engagement is dropping," or "should Jon post this or should the brand." For an individual video script see reels-scripts; for a dated schedule see content-calendar; for paid amplification of the same creative see paid-social; for Jon's on-camera voice see coach-brand-voice.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which accounts exist, what has been posted, what the honest current baseline is, who can film

Frameworks > Platform mechanics (Tier A/B sourced): watch time as the entry ticket, sends and shares per reach as the scaling lever weighted well above likes, saves driving carousel distribution. State the tier next to every number and forbid restating any of it publicly

Frameworks > Format economics table: carousels ~0.50%, Reels ~0.48%, images ~0.33% engagement rate (Socialinsider 35M-post benchmark, Tier A), median cadence 8 Reels / 5 carousels / 7 images per month. Read: Reels buy reach, carousels buy trust, statics are the weakest slot
Frameworks > The share test: design every Reel so one specific person would DM it to one specific friend. "Send this to the person who keeps restarting Monday" beats "double tap if you agree"
Frameworks > Five content pillars mapped to hubs, with the mechanism each proves and the format it wants
Frameworks > Account architecture: brand account vs coach account, what each owns, how they cross-post
Output buckets: Decisions locked / Weekly operating cadence / Pillar-to-format matrix / Measurement / Open questions
Become-specific rules: no viral-only strategy, no engagement bait, no results claims, no before/after

name: reels-scripts
description: Writes shootable short-form video scripts for Reels, TikTok, and Shorts — a hook that lands inside the first 1.5 seconds, a beat-by-beat shot list with cut timings, on-screen text that says something different from the spoken line, a loop-close, and a CTA that is not "link in bio" — plus slide-by-slide carousel decks when the idea reads better as stills, all built around real Become mechanics like whole-plate photo logging, the equipment-aware session generator, and the weekly recap. Use when the user says "write a reel," "script a TikTok," "we need a hook," "make a video about the photo food logging," "write a carousel," "30 second video idea," "turn this feature into a video," or "this reel flopped, fix it." For the cadence and pillar decisions behind it see social-strategy; for a creator filming it see ugc-creator-briefs; for rendering a motion asset instead of filming see remotion-assets.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which mechanism is the payoff, who films it, what footage or capture already exists, target length
Frameworks > Length bands: 15-30s highest completion, 21-34s most shares, 11-18s skews viral, 45-60s+ for teaching, 30-45s the most repurposable cut for paid

Frameworks > The first 1.5 seconds as production rules, not statistics: frame one holds a face, a motion, or a legible 4-7 word overlay. Never a logo, never a title card, never a slow push-in. No "hey guys." Spoken hook and on-screen text carry different information. Cut or reframe every 1.5-2.5s for the first 8 seconds. Last frame rhymes with the first to earn replays

Frameworks > Six script archetypes with a full worked example each: the App Tip how-to sequence (the strongest pattern in our inspo library), the mechanism demo, the misconception flip, the day-in-the-plan, the coach answer, the recap reveal
Frameworks > Hook matrix: ten hook shapes crossed with the hubs, with weak-vs-strong pairs
Output buckets: The script (timecoded beats, VO, on-screen text, b-roll) / Annotations / Two alternate hooks / Capture list naming exact files or the screenshot-capture run needed
Become-specific rules: film real screens only; no fabricated results; no shaming hooks; The Becoming is at most one beat

name: content-calendar
description: Turns pillars and campaigns into a dated, sourced publishing calendar — what posts on which day, in which format, on which platform, from which existing asset or capture, with a repeatable weekly template and named recurring slots. Every row names the asset it needs and the skill that produces it, so nothing is scheduled that cannot be shot. Use when the user says "build a content calendar," "what are we posting this month," "plan the week," "we keep scrambling for content," "batch our posts," "give me 30 days of content," or "we have nothing queued." For the pillar and cadence decisions upstream see social-strategy; for the individual script see reels-scripts; for a launch week specifically see launch-campaign.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: date range, realistic production capacity, what already exists in marketing/out and screenshots/v2, what is shipping in the product this month
Frameworks > The weekly template: fixed slots by day, each bound to a pillar and format, with named recurring slots (the inspo library shows a named-slot pattern works)
Frameworks > Batch production: one capture session and one film session feed a month

Frameworks > Asset sourcing rules, in preference order: existing render in marketing/out, existing capture in screenshots/v2, new render via remotion-assets, new capture via screenshot-capture, new film via reels-scripts or ugc-creator-briefs
Frameworks > Calendar row schema (date, platform, format, pillar, hook, asset path or producing skill, caption owner, status)
Output buckets: Decisions locked / The calendar table / Assets required with producing skill / Batch plan / Open questions
Become-specific rules: never schedule a post that needs a capture nobody has agreed to shoot; never schedule around a feature that has not shipped

name: ugc-creator-briefs
description: Writes briefs for creators, members, and affiliates filming Become content — deliverable spec and usage rights, hook direction, must-show product moments, shot list, a do-not-say list, FTC disclosure requirements, and the approval checklist that keeps captured footage inside our constraints. Use when the user says "brief a creator," "we're working with an influencer," "UGC brief," "what should the creator say," "can we repost this member's video," "do they have to say ad," "send them the rules," or "we got a video, can we use it." No fabricated testimonial, invented result, or price claim may enter through creator content, and permission is required before any member content is reposted. For Jon's own first-person voice see coach-brand-voice; for the beat structure of the video itself see reels-scripts; for paid amplification of creator assets see paid-social.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: paid or gifted or organic, deliverable count and format, usage window and paid-amplification rights, who approves
Frameworks > The brief template, section by section: context, audience, the one idea, hook direction, must-show moments, shot list, do-not-say list, disclosure, deliverable spec, timeline, rights

Frameworks > FTC disclosure rules: material connection disclosed clearly and conspicuously, in the video and in the caption, "#ad" or "paid partnership" not buried, disclosure applies to gifted access too

Frameworks > The do-not-say list for fitness creators: no medical claims, no promised pounds or timelines, no before/after implying a guarantee, no "this cured my X," no invented pricing, no naming a competitor negatively
Frameworks > Member content and reposting: written permission, no minors, no camera-roll body photos, no screenshot of another user's data
Output buckets: The brief / Annotations / Alternate hook directions / Approval checklist
Become-specific rules: creator claims are our claims; the constraint list applies to their words too

name: coach-brand-voice
description: Defines and writes Jon Don's first-person coach voice for anything fronted by him — talking-head scripts, captions, direct-to-camera openers, member replies, story answers, DM and comment responses, and coaching one-liners — and keeps that register cleanly separate from the product's second-person voice. Use when the user says "write this as Jon," "make it sound like the coach," "Jon's caption," "what would the coach say," "this doesn't sound like him," "reply to this comment," or "we need a founder post." Enforces the no-personal-camera-roll-photos rule and the responsible-claims limits on everything attributed to a real person. For the product's own voice see copywriting; for the video structure around his words see reels-scripts; for creators who are not Jon see ugc-creator-briefs.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: is this Jon or the brand speaking, which surface, is it a reply to a real person, is any claim being made about a client

Frameworks > The two registers side by side: product (second person, present tense, mechanism-first) vs coach (first person, experience-first, direct address). Table with the same message written both ways
Frameworks > Jon's voice rules: says what he would say to a client in the gym, gives the reason not just the rule, admits tradeoffs, never shames, never hypes, never promises an outcome
Frameworks > Reply patterns: acknowledge, answer concretely, one next step. With ❌/✅ pairs for real comment types (skeptic, beginner, injury question, price question, competitor comparison)
Frameworks > Injury, medical, and pregnancy questions: the referral response and why it is non-negotiable
Frameworks > Coach credibility as proof: what he has actually built is the proof, not numbers we do not have
Output buckets: The copy / Annotations / Two alternates (shorter, warmer) / Anything needing Jon's sign-off
Become-specific rules: never invent a client story, a client result, or a personal anecdote

name: email-lifecycle
description: Designs and writes Become's email program — the magic-link and verification transactional set, the welcome and activation sequence, week-one habit emails, the weekly recap send, lapsed-user win-back, and re-engagement — with subject lines, preview text, send timing, trigger and suppression logic, and plain deliverable HTML because sending runs through Nodemailer SMTP. Use when the user says "write a welcome email," "our emails don't get opened," "win-back sequence," "email people who haven't logged a workout," "what should the recap email say," "set up onboarding emails," or "the magic link email looks bad." For in-app and browser nudges see push-notifications; for the activation flow the emails support see signup-activation; for the launch announcement send see launch-campaign.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which lifecycle stage, what triggers it, what data the app actually has to personalize it, what the single action is

Frameworks > The lifecycle map: transactional (magic link, verify), activation (day 0-7), habit (weekly recap, streak), reactivation (7/14/30-day lapse), broadcast (launch, program drop). Each with trigger, timing, goal metric, and suppression
Frameworks > The magic-link email itself: deliverability, subject clarity, one button, expiry stated, what to do if it was not you. This is the highest-stakes email we send
Frameworks > Subject line and preview text craft with weak-vs-strong pairs and length specs
Frameworks > Recap emails from real data: workouts logged, volume, streak, mood trend, calories hit. Never a metric the user did not generate
Frameworks > Deliverability under SMTP: plain structure, low image weight, real from-name, one link domain, unsubscribe on non-transactional
Output buckets: The sequence table / Full copy per email / Annotations / Subject line alternates / Suppression rules
Become-specific rules: no fake urgency, no guilt subject lines, no pricing, no promised results

name: push-notifications
description: Writes and schedules Become's web push notifications — permission-prompt timing and copy, the daily nudge set, streak and recap triggers, workout-day reminders, quiet hours, frequency caps, and a visible opt-out — tuned to a PWA where one badly timed prompt loses the channel permanently. Use when the user says "write a push notification," "when should we ask for notification permission," "our notifications are annoying," "streak reminder copy," "people are turning off push," "nudge users who missed a workout," or "can we send a push for this." Web push exists in Become today and there is no native app, so browser permission rules govern everything. For longer-form messaging see email-lifecycle; for the habit loop the nudges serve see signup-activation; for the behavioural principles behind them see marketing-psychology.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: what user state triggers this, what the user gets by tapping, is this the best channel or should it be email, what happens if they ignore it
Frameworks > Permission prompt: never on first load, never a browser prompt without a pre-prompt, ask after the first earned win, explain what they will get, allow "not now" without penalty

Frameworks > The nudge inventory: workout-day reminder, missed-session recovery, streak-at-risk, weekly recap ready, mood check-in, water and nutrition targets, program phase change. Each with trigger, timing window, cap, and copy
Frameworks > Copy specs: title character budget, body character budget, one action, no ALL CAPS, no emoji spam, the notification must be true at the moment it fires
Frameworks > Frequency, quiet hours, and the do-not-disturb rules; how to decay nudges for a user who ignores them
Frameworks > Never-shame rule with ❌/✅ pairs on streak-at-risk copy, the highest-risk category
Output buckets: The nudge table / Full copy per nudge / Annotations / Alternates / Trigger and cap spec
Become-specific rules: never fabricate a stat inside a push; never guilt; every push must be dismissible without cost

name: launch-campaign
description: Plans and runs a single Become launch moment — a feature launch like whole-plate photo logging or the AI session generator, a program drop, a directory submission, or a relaunch — using an owned, rented, and borrowed channel split, a readiness gate that stops a premature launch, a day-by-day run of show, the asset manifest, and the post-launch review. Use when the user says "we're launching X," "launch plan," "how do we announce this," "Product Hunt launch," "big feature drop next week," "nobody noticed our last launch," or "we shipped something, now what." For the standing plan this fits inside see marketing-plan; for the directory listings themselves see web-app-listing; for the dated posts see content-calendar; for the announcement email see email-lifecycle.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: what actually shipped and is it stable on production, who is the launch for, what does success mean, what is the single date

Frameworks > The readiness gate: feature works on mobile in light and dark, captures exist and show no bug or empty state, the landing page mentions it, tracking is in place, support answer written. No gate, no launch

Frameworks > Owned / Rented / Borrowed: owned (landing, email list, push, in-app), rented (social accounts, directories), borrowed (Jon's audience, creators, communities, press). Sequence and expected contribution of each
Frameworks > Run of show: T-14 through T+7, with the owner and asset per row
Frameworks > Directory and community launch etiquette: what gets you removed from a subreddit or a Product Hunt front page
Output buckets: Decisions locked / Run of show table / Assets required with producing skill / Success metrics / Post-launch review template
Become-specific rules: never launch on a feature not live on become.redbtn.io; never launch with "(beta)" visible in a capture; no invented launch-day pricing or discount

name: referral-program

name: seo-geo

name: ab-testing
description: Designs and reads marketing experiments for Become — turning an observation into a falsifiable hypothesis, choosing a primary metric and guardrails, sizing the test honestly against low traffic, sequencing tests by expected value, and calling a result without fooling ourselves. Use when the user says "A/B test this," "which headline wins," "run an experiment," "is this result significant," "we don't have enough traffic to test," "should we test or just ship," "the test looks positive," or "how long do we run it." At our volume it will often recommend shipping the better-reasoned version and measuring sequentially instead of running an underpowered split. For the page changes worth testing see landing-cro; for the events behind the metric see analytics-tracking; for creative testing inside ad platforms see paid-social.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: current baseline conversion, weekly traffic, minimum effect worth detecting, how long we are willing to wait
Frameworks > Hypothesis format: because [evidence], we believe [change] will cause [metric] to [direction] for [segment], measured by [event], and we are wrong if [guardrail]
Frameworks > Sizing honestly: the sample-size intuition table (baseline rate x detectable lift x weeks required at our traffic). When the answer is "never," say so

Frameworks > The low-traffic playbook: sequential shipping with pre and post windows, painted-door and demand tests, qualitative session review, five-second tests, and why big swings beat button colours
Frameworks > Calling a result: peeking, novelty effects, segment fishing, guardrail regressions, and the write-up template
Frameworks > The test backlog: scoring by expected value and effort, not by curiosity
Output buckets: Hypothesis / Test design / Sizing verdict (run it, ship it, or skip it) / Analysis plan / Decision rule agreed in advance
Become-specific rules: two channels share one database, so any test must isolate by channel or route; never test anything that degrades a real user's health data

name: paid-social

name: marketing-psychology
description: Applies behavioural principles to Become's marketing and product surfaces — loss aversion around streaks, endowed progress and the fresh-start effect, identity-based habit framing, social proof we can honestly use, friction and default design, and the Zeigarnik pull of an unfinished week — with an explicit line between persuasion and manipulation. Use when the user says "why don't people convert," "make this more persuasive," "psychology of habit apps," "how do streaks actually work," "is this dark-pattern-y," "what makes people come back," or "is this urgency manipulative." Every technique is checked against the no-shaming, no-fabrication, and responsible-claims rules before it is recommended. For applying it to the page see landing-cro; for the nudge copy see push-notifications; for the offer framing see offer-design.
sections_hint: Process assessment gate: which behaviour are we trying to change, is the barrier motivation or ability or trigger, is the honest version of this technique available to us

Frameworks > Principles ranked by fit for Become, each with Check-for / Common issues / Strong patterns and a Become application: identity and self-signalling, endowed progress, loss aversion on streaks, fresh start effect, Zeigarnik and the unfinished week, implementation intentions, social proof without numbers, defaults and friction, peak-end for the weekly recap

Frameworks > The manipulation line: a technique is legitimate if the user would still endorse it after it is explained. Table of dark patterns we refuse (confirmshaming, fake scarcity, roach-motel opt-out, guilt streaks, forced continuity)
Frameworks > Honest social proof for a product with no counts to show: mechanism proof, coach credibility, real product captures, member words only with permission
Frameworks > Streaks done responsibly: streak repair, no punishment, no public loss
Output buckets: Diagnosis / Techniques recommended with the principle named / Copy or UX changes / What we refuse and why
Become-specific rules: users are not lazy, their tools were scattered; never shame; never fabricate proof to trigger a bias

name: screenshot-capture
